title.narrative: Integrated Health, Nutrition to Mitigate Lean Season Vulnerability in Dikwa Madagali LGAs

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to deliver an integrated and comprehensive package of lifesaving health, nutrition interventions targeting 27,000 vulnerable individuals in Dikwa, Borno State and 12,000 in Madagali, Adamawa State during the 2025 lean season. HARAF and SRF will jointly deliver interventions targeting 15,000 individuals with health, 12,000 with nutrition. HARAF is coordinating all the activities through the sub-IP. Through the strengthening of one health facilities, deployment of two mobile medical teams and two RCCE team for the purpose of sensitization and awraenesss creation. the initiative will reduce preventable morbidity and mortality among children under five, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), and other at-risk groups. The project combines outpatient consultations, maternal and reproductive health services, nutrition screening and treatment, cholera/malaria surveillance, and risk communication to ensure equitable access for populations in hard-to-reach and underserved areas. In Dikwa, humanitarian needs have sharply escalated following the September 2024 Alau Dam collapse, which flooded vast areas, destroyed farmland, displaced households, and damaged health infrastructure. Over 350,000 people were displaced across Borno due to flooding, compounding the impact of conflict and displacement on already fragile health systems. At the same time, the withdrawal of USAID nutrition support in early 2025 left over 400,000 displaced people without critical health and nutrition services, with INTERSOS, the only remaining provider scaling down operations despite surging needs. Outbreaks of cholera, malaria, and diarrheal disease remain high risks due to overcrowding and poor WASH conditions, while SRH service availability is severely constrained. In Madagali, displacement from conflict, compounded by seasonal food insecurity, continues to strain overstretched health and nutrition systems. The 2024 Sectoral Needs and Risk Analysis (SNRA) highlighted Madagali as one of the LGAs with high vulnerability due to malnutrition, limited access to safe water, and health service gaps. Children under five and PLW face increasing risks of acute malnutrition with BAY states projected to see 2.6 million acutely malnourished children in 2025, including 1 million SAM cases. Nutrition interventions in Madagali will therefore focus on community-level screening, SAM/MAM treatment, and MIYCN counselling, alongside hygiene and feeding education. By combining facility-based care with mobile outreach, this project ensures a continuum of services that directly align with NHF SA2 2025 priorities: lifesaving health and nutrition interventions, early detection and outbreak response, and community-centered service delivery. The intervention integrates Protection Mainstreaming, AAP, gender equality, disability inclusion, and PSEA measures throughout, ensuring accountability and safety for affected populations while strengthening resilience during the lean season. ltbrgtConclusively, it is a mandate from HARAF and the subIP to coordinate and work with the BSPHCDA go strengthen the linkages of the state health systems to support sustainability by doing the following:ltbrgtAdaptation of the state data tools for monthly reporting.ltbrgtCapacity building of facility staffs before the commencement of the project as well as on the job training and support.ltbrgtWorking along side the LGA level coordination team and other partners.ltbrgtSupport the joint monitoring and supervision quarterly to all sites of working.ltbrgtlt/pgt
